title: stabilization-runloop-rotation-index-and-customer-briefs-2024
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the Stabilization Runloop used for first 90 minutes of an operational incident, the Responder Rotation Index (role matrix and handover rules), a compact Evidence Cookbook for collecting defensible data during live incidents, plus ready-to-send customer-facing status templates for the status page and email/Slack.

Scope: Applies to all incidents impacting Redwood hosted inference, dedicated pools, or private deployments where customer-visible SLOs (latency, availability, embeddings correctness) are degraded. This is not a replacement for per-service runbooks; it is the cross-service stabilization scaffold to be used for multi-service degradations and escalations.

Ownership and contacts

- Incident Commander (IC): role assigned per incident, default escalation to oncall SRE.
- Bridge Operator: Engineering oncall who manages the bridge/Slack channel and status updates.
- Service Stewards: owners of affected services (listed in service catalog).
- Evidence Custodian: the investigator responsible for capturing and preserving logs/traces/artifacts.

If IC unknown, page on-call rota: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/oncall-rotations-index (canonical).

Stabilization Runloop (0–90 minute scaffold)

1) First 5 minutes — Acknowledge & classify
   - Acknowledge pager and immediately open incident bridge (Zoom/Slack Huddle).
   - IC posts short incident summary to #incidents and triggers the Notification Ladder.
   - Classify impact: Severity-1 (Service down), Severity-2 (SLO degradation), Severity-3 (partial/isolated).
   - Record initial hypothesis (one-line) and begin Evidence Cookbook checklist.

2) Minutes 5–20 — Contain and prioritize
   - IC defines containment objective (e.g., prevent error amplification, reduce traffic, disable problematic route).
   - Apply safe mitigations: route failover, short-term rate limits, circuit-breakers, scaling spot instances.
   - Bridge Operator posts customer-facing interim message (see templates).

3) Minutes 20–45 — Diagnose and validate mitigation
   - Evidence Custodian collects logs, trace IDs, request/response samples, and KV-cache snapshot if applicable.
   - Attach diagnostics to incident ticket (Incident ID).
   - If mitigation effective, transition to ‘stabilized’ state and monitor for recurrence for 30–60 minutes.

4) Minutes 45–90 — Remediate and prepare recovery steps
   - Plan rollback or patching steps if mitigation is temporary.
   - If code or model change is implicated, freeze further rollouts and enable model fallback to previous verified variant.
   - IC schedules follow-up action owners and post-incident blameless RCA lead.

Rotation Index: Roles & Handoff Rules

- Incident Commander (IC): single owner for decision authority. Handover rule: new IC must be explicitly accepted on the bridge and announce time of handover.
- Bridge Operator: responsible for status messages, stakeholder pings, and customer notices. Handover rule: share latest message draft and last timestamp of customer update.
- Technical Lead(s): service-specific engineers. Handover rule: summarize tests run and next required action.
- Evidence Custodian: ensures artifacts are stored and preserved. Handover rule: provide storage path and list of preserved artifacts.

Handover checklist (always read out loud on bridge):
1. Active mitigations (what, who, when applied)
2. Observed impact and metrics at handover
3. Pending actions and blockers
4. Next scheduled status update time

Evidence Cookbook (what to collect, where, and why)

Collect early, collect often. Preserve raw artifacts before running destructive remediation when possible. If live remediation must occur, snapshot before mutation.

Minimum artifact set (Evidence Custodian priority):
- Incident ID and timeline (UTC).
- Pager payload and originating alert rule.
- Top 100 error logs (timestamped) from affected services (JSON format).
- Representative request/response pairs with headers and model outputs (redact user PII).
- Trace spans (trace IDs) covering failure path (link to APM dashboard).
- Token-level runtime metrics for LLM requests (latency, tokens emitted, backend queue time).
- KV cache stats and recent cache hit/miss samples (if applicable).
- GPU/host telemetry at incident window (GPU utilization, memory, XLA failures).
- Rollout/CI history for the last 24h (deploy IDs, model version, quantization profile).
- Network flow captures or LB logs if packet-level issues suspected.

Storage and retention
- Upload artifacts to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/{incident-id}/evidence (or internal equivalent).
- Tag artifacts with incident-id and evidence-custodian name.
- Retain critical artifacts for 90 days by default; escalate to security if retention needed longer for compliance.

Chain of custody notes: record who pulled/exported data and the precise commands used. Example:
- Command: aws s3 cp /var/log/service/error.log s3://redwood-incidents/INC-1234/evidence/error.log --profile incident-custodian

Postmortem & Blameless RCA process

Triggers for postmortem:
- Any customer-visible SLO breach lasting > 5 minutes.
- Any incident with an SLA credit or legal/regulatory impact.

Postmortem template (must be filled within 7 business days):
1. Summary: 3-sentence incident synopsis and customer impact.
2. Timeline: concise, minute-level timeline of key events.
3. Root cause: single sentence plus supporting evidence.
4. Contributing factors: systemic/process/code/model items.
5. Remediations: short-term and long-term with owners and ETA.
6. Follow-ups: list of tracked action items in Jira with owners.
7. Lessons learned and monitoring improvements.

Game-days and simulation guidance

Objectives for exercises:
- Validate Stabilization Runloop timings (ack -> bridge -> first customer notice).
- Exercise Evidence Cookbook collection under time pressure.
- Verify rotation handovers and noisy-channel reduction (fewer than 3 concurrent messengers).

Recommended scenarios (quarterly):
- KV-cache mismatch causing degraded latency for tail queries.
- Model rollout causing hallucination/regression in a targeted prompt set.
- Multiregion failover with partial capacity loss in a primary region.

Scoring rubric:
- Time-to-first-bridge (target < 4 minutes)
- Time-to-interim-customer-notice (target < 15 minutes)
- Evidence completeness (required artifacts captured)
- Number of simultaneous communicators (target 1–2)

Status Page & Customer Brief Templates

Use plain, non-technical language for public pages. Keep customer notices short, factual, and updated at predictable cadence (every 15–30 minutes while active).

Public status page template (short):
- Title: Incident: High Latency for Model Generation
- Short summary: We are investigating increased latency for text generation in our hosted API. Some requests may return slowly or time out.
- Impact: A subset of customers in us-west-2 may see generation latency over 5s.
- ETA: We are actively diagnosing; next update in 30 minutes.
- Mitigation: We have applied a temporary routing change to reduce error amplification.

Customer email/Slack brief (interim):
- Subject: Redwood status update — degraded inference latency (Incident INC-1234)
- Body: Hello — We are investigating a latency issue affecting text generation. Our engineers have applied a temporary routing change and are collecting diagnostics. We will post another update in 30 minutes. If you rely on low-latency endpoints, please consider using the regional failover option or pinning to dedicated capacity.

Internal short message (Bridge Operator to #incidents):
- [INC-1234] S2: High tail latency RN. Mitigation applied: routing to fallback pool. Evidence custodian: @sam. Next update: +30m.

Escalation Ladder (summary)

1. Oncall SRE (automated pager)
2. Service Steward and Technical Lead
3. Senior SRE (on-call escalation)
4. Head of Platform (for customer SLA/regulatory impact)

SLO & alert thresholds (examples)

- Generation latency p95 > 2s for 2 minutes: P1 alert to oncall (Pager).
- Error rate > 5% for 5 minutes: P1 alert.
- KV cache eviction rate spike > 10x baseline for 60s: P2 alert.

Runbook snippets (examples to copy into service runbooks)

- Rotate service to fallback pool:
  curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/services/{service}/route -d '{"pool":"fallback-1"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"

- Snapshot recent logs (last 30 minutes):
  journalctl -u redwood-service --since "30 minutes ago" -o json > /tmp/redwood-logs-INC-1234.json

- Export trace spans for ID TRACE-####:
  apm-cli export --trace-id TRACE-#### --out s3://redwood-incidents/INC-1234/evidence/trace-TRACE-####.json

Appendix: Helpful links and templates
